- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a spike in price (e.g., >45), model tends to overshoot and stay high; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., >0.3) mid-period, model often underreacts — increase forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend in forecast vs true, adjust next forecast to align with 20-day moving average.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–5% to avoid momentum overfit.  
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underpredicts — add 2–5% buffer to forecast to account for volatility.
